memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: If someone is found slain, lying in a field in the land the Lord your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who the killer was, your elders and judges shall go out and measure the distance from the body to the neighboring towns. - Deut 21:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God addresses a heartbreaking situation, a person found murdered in a field, with no one knowing who did it. In many societies, such a death would simply be ignored. No suspect, no case, no justice. But not so with God. He commands the elders and judges to go out, measure the distances, and take the matter seriously. The unsolved death of one person mattered to God.

Think about what this reveals. God does not overlook the forgotten victim. Even when human justice cannot identify the guilty party, God will not let innocent blood be treated as worthless. The life of that unknown person, lying alone in a field, was precious to the God who made them.

This is deeply comforting. We live in a world full of injustices that never seem to be resolved, wrongs that go unpunished, victims who seem forgotten. But God sees every one. Not a single injustice escapes His notice, and He will one day set all things right. Nothing is hidden from His sight (Heb 4:13). If you have ever felt like a forgotten victim, or grieved over injustice that no one else seems to notice, take heart. The God who cared about a body in a field cares about you and every wrong done to you. Do you trust that God sees what others overlook?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you believe God sees the injustices others ignore?
2. Where have you felt forgotten or overlooked?
3. How does God's attention to the unseen comfort you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You see every forgotten victim and every hidden wrong. Help me trust that You will set all things right in Your time. Amen.
